cases.q: how quick is it when paying notes out one after another?
cases.reference: The NV4000 uses spray payout with note-to-note dispense times of less than 2 seconds.

cases.q: how many notes does the refill cassette hold and can i mix denominations in it
cases.reference: The replenishment cassette holds 400 notes of mixed denominations and can be used either to refill the recycling drums or for direct payment. It discriminates notes but they are presumed to be staff-verified, genuine and fit.

cases.q: nv4000 earth bonding - whats the max resistance to earth we're allowed?
cases.reference: The resistance between the chassis and earth must be less than 0.7 ohms. On the standard chassis the earth tab goes to the lower screw mounting points at the side; with a replenishment cassette, the 4 mounting holes on the bottom of the cassette can be used.

cases.q: What's the peak current the unit can pull? sizing the supply for a kiosk
cases.reference: Supply current varies with the phase of operation; the maximum the device can draw is 7 A. The setup examples call for a stable 24 VDC / 7 A supply.

cases.q: which PSU do you recommend for this? I'd like to just order one off RS
cases.reference: The manual suggests the TDK Lambda RWS-300B-24 (+24 VDC / 12.5 A), RS stock code 813-9128 (Farnell 2419997). The supply must be an ES1 source to IEC/UL 62368-1 or SELV to IEC/UL 60950-1.

cases.q: what connector is on the recycler for power + serial comms?
cases.reference: A 16-pin Molex 0039012165 connector on top of the NV4000 carries power and TTL, RS-232 and opto-isolated interfacing, next to a USB Type B socket. Power is always needed on pins 15 (+V) and 16 (0V).

cases.q: how much internal storage is there for the event logs
cases.reference: The NV200 Spectral head in the NV4000 has 128MB of internal memory for event and performance logs.

cases.q: staff keep dropping the nv4000 cashbox when they empty it. what drop is it actually designed to survive?
cases.reference: The cashbox is designed to stay intact after a 75 cm drop onto a concrete floor. Repeated drops can still damage it physically.

cases.q: units have been sat in a freezing warehouse, how fast can i warm them up before switching on?
cases.reference: Going from storage to operating temperature should be done no faster than 2°C per hour.

cases.q: putting one in an unheated kiosk. whats the coldest it can run at? humidity gets pretty high there as well
cases.reference: Operating range is +3°C to +50°C at 5% to 95% humidity, non-condensing. Storage allows 0°C to +60°C, but that is not for operation.

cases.q: our 24v rail sags to about 21.2V when everything's running. is that within spec?
cases.reference: No. The minimum supply voltage is +21.6 VDC (nominal +24 VDC, maximum +26.4 VDC), with ripple no more than 0.25 V at 100 Hz.

cases.q: max note width for loading thru the replenishment cassette?
cases.reference: Notes entering through the replenishment cassette must be 60-79 mm wide and 110-165 mm long, narrower than the 85 mm the validator takes. Wider notes such as Euro 100, 200 and 500 series 1 won't fit; only insert the series 2 versions.

cases.q: the validator takes our 84mm wide notes no problem. can those notes go into the recycler drums too?
cases.reference: No. Notes sent to the recyclers can be at most 82 mm wide (60-82 mm, length 110-165 mm), even though the validator accepts notes up to 85 mm wide.

cases.q: what size screws for mounting the bezel and the cashbox
cases.reference: Bezel: M3 thread, 12 mm long. Cashbox: M4 thread, 6 mm long. Machine-mounting screws are not included in the delivery.

cases.q: our host board drives its outputs at 3.3V. will the nv4000 inputs read that as high?
cases.reference: Probably not: input logic high is +3.7 V to +12 V and logic low is 0 to +0.5 V, so 3.3 V is below the logic-high minimum. Outputs are +0.6 V low with a 2K2 pull-up and can sink at most 50 mA each.

cases.q: bezel is flashing 1 red then 2 blue, what do i do
cases.reference: 1 red / 2 blue is a note path jam: the note hasn't reached the recycler side and is in the head, between the head and the interface, or between the interface and the cashbox. If it's in the note path, lift the front latch, pull the validator towards you, open the head release catch, carefully remove the note, then shut the head and re-dock. If it's in the interface, slide the red latch forward to hinge the door up. If it's sticking out of the cashbox, disconnect power, remove the head and wind the drive gears on the left.

cases.q: Got a recycler jam, pulled the stuck note out of the drum and put it all back together. Anything else I should do before going back in service?
cases.reference: Yes. After clearing a recycler jam, run an empty on that recycler and then re-float it; the manual warns that skipping the empty can cause further issues. It's also recommended to test with about 10 notes in and 10 out.
must_include: run an empty on that recycler

cases.q: how do i load a new dataset off an sd card
cases.reference: Use a blank FAT-32 card (4-32GB, Class 10) and create a lowercase folder called nv200hs containing the dataset file. With the unit powered and booted, insert the card in the front slot; the bezel flashes. Don't unplug it, wait for solid green, then remove the card. The unit reboots (about 10 s) and then updates the NV4000 modules.

cases.q: ITL support want logs off our nv4000. how do i pull them
cases.reference: Insert a FAT-32 SD card with an empty folder named NV200SL in the front slot. The bezel flashes alternating colours and turns green when the transfer is done; then remove the card. A blank FAT-32 card also works: it creates the folders and grabs the internal log.

cases.q: acceptance has gone downhill, how should i clean the validator? ok to use isopropyl wipes?
cases.reference: No alcohol or other solvents, which can permanently damage the unit. Disconnect power, remove the head (lift the red head release catch, slide forward, lift off) and open the note path cover (ideally remove the bezel too). Wipe with a soft lint-free cloth dampened, not wet, with water and mild detergent, make sure the lenses are clean and dry, and don't lubricate anything. Clean the optical lenses monthly or as required.

cases.q: conveyor module leds: green flashing, red blinks once, orange blinks twice. what is that
cases.reference: On the conveyor module, flashing green with red 1 / orange 2 means Belt Missing.

cases.q: host software cant see the recycler at all, its hooked up through an IF17. where do i start
cases.reference: Check the IF17 connectors are fully seated and its USB cable is connected to the PC. In Windows Device Manager look for a USB Serial Port; if none appears, replace the IF17. If there is still no connection, replace the IF17 or switch COM ports. A yellow triangle on the port means reinstall the drivers; on Linux use dmesg.
must_include: USB Serial Port in Device Manager

cases.q: can I run the 2200 note cashbox together with the replenishment cassette?
cases.reference: No. The 2200 note cashbox inner (PA03109) and its chassis (PA03296) cannot be used with the replenishment cassette option.
must_include: 2200 cashbox not compatible with replenishment cassette

cases.q: if im only talking to it over usb do i still need the 24v hooked up on the 16 pin?
cases.reference: Yes. +24 VDC (pin 15) and 0V (pin 16) must always be connected, including when using USB.

cases.q: do we have to pay for validator manager / the nv4000 firmware downloads?
cases.reference: No. All ITL software is free of charge; you download it from the website after registering and logging in.

cases.q: how long does it keep a note in escrow before handing it back to the customer?
cases.reference: The NV4000 manual does not mention escrow or an escrow timeout.

cases.q: whats the IP rating? looking at putting it in an outdoor car park pay station
cases.reference: The NV4000 manual gives no IP or ingress-protection rating and says nothing about outdoor use; it lists only temperature and humidity ranges.

cases.q: does it have an internal battery backup so it can finish a payout if the mains goes?
cases.reference: The NV4000 manual does not mention any battery backup or how the unit behaves when power fails.

cases.q: all our NV200 Spectrals run off a 12V supply. can the nv4000 go on the same 12v rail?
cases.reference: No. The NV4000 needs +24 VDC (21.6-26.4 VDC). The NV200 Spectral accepts either 12 V (10.8-13.2 VDC) or 24 V (21.6-26.4 VDC).

cases.q: this takes our 168mm long notes fine. if we move to the NV4000 will it still accept them?
cases.reference: No. The NV4000 accepts notes 110-165 mm long (60-85 mm wide) through its validator, while the NV200 Spectral manual allows 110-170 mm (56-85 mm wide), so a 168 mm note is outside the NV4000 spec.

cases.q: we've got a stack of 4GB class 4 sd cards we use for updating the nv200 spectrals. will those work for the nv4000?
cases.reference: No. The NV4000 needs at least a 4GB Class 10 card (maximum 32GB Class 10). The NV200 Spectral minimum is 4GB Class 4, which is why those cards work there.

cases.q: MCBF on the NV4000 vs a plain NV200 Spectral?
cases.reference: The NV4000 targets an MCBF of 100,000 (MCBI 25,000). The NV200 Spectral MCBF is 200,000 cycles, halved for each additional module attached.

cases.turn1: how do I flash new firmware onto the nv4000 with validator manager?
cases.q: what if the pc crashes halfway thru
cases.reference: Interrupting the download can leave the unit in a non-functional state, and once started the process cannot be halted.

cases.turn1: need to fit a key lock on the front of the validator head, how do i do it?
cases.q: whats the part number for the lock so i can order a few
cases.reference: The NV200 Spectral lock is ITL part number PA00650. A keyless lock assembly, PA02713, is also available and comes as standard on the 1000 note cashbox.

cases.turn1: if a note jams while the nv4000 is paying out to a customer, whose money is it?
cases.q: and what if it jams while refilling from the cassette?
cases.reference: During a replenish, if the cassette is treated separately from the main system's money (for example an external refill company), the note isn't classed as stored until it has fully entered the recycler, so it can be treated as the replenisher's. This is guidance only; integrators can handle it as they choose.
must_include: not stored until fully in the recycler

cases.q: does the NV4000 Lite still take the 400 note replenishment cassette or is that only on the full one?
cases.reference: There is no NV4000 Lite in the documentation; the manual covers only the NV4000 range with its modular options.
